sentences.text:
Hariram Lodhi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 September,
2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Gwl:20740
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Gwalior
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Rajesh Kumar Gupta
 On The 8 th Of September, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 30730 of 2025
 Hariram Lodhi
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Shri Sooraj Bhan Lodhi - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Saket Udeniya - Pp for the State.

Order 
This is first application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of the BNSS for grant of regular bail.
The applicant has been arrested in connection with Crime No.195/2025 registered at Police Station Karera, District Shivpuri for offence under Sections 420, 467, 471 of IPC.
2. Allegation against the present applicant is that he was involved in misappropriate of money and was also instrumental in conspiracy by way of committing fraud in sale of the disputed land.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated.
He is in custody since 29.06.2025.
It is further contended that the applicant is neither the land owner nor he has received any money in the aforesaid sale transaction.
He was only a witnesses in the aforesaid incident.

At best, it is a case of civil nature, which NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20740 2 MCRC-30730-2025 has been given color of the criminal case and still the present applicant is not a part of any conspiracy or misdeed in the sale transaction of the disputed land.
There is no criminal antecedent against the present applicant.
Charge- sheet has been filed and the investigation is over, therefore, custodial interrogation is no longer required.
Applicant is a permanent resident of District Shivpuri (M.P.), therefore, there is no possibility of his absconsion or tampering with the prosecution evidence.
Applicant undertakes to cooperate in trial as well as the investigation and would make himself available as and when required.
Under these grounds, counsel prayed for bail.
4. On the other hand, learned State counsel vehemently opposed the bail application and prayed for its rejection.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, but without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, this application is allowed and it is directed that the applicant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) along with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court/Committal Court.
